purpose: Attack the largest remaining RC1 evidence gap by grounding a K1 regression witness in an actual black-box implementation execution without modifying RC1, W0, W1, or W2 and without laundering black-box testing into preservation authority.

core_asymmetry.regression: One independently observed forbidden consequence at the declared consequential cut may ground a regression witness.
core_asymmetry.preservation: No finite set of black-box executions in B0 may establish preservation or target closure. Absence of an observed forbidden consequence yields no semantic authority.

qualification_restriction.reason: Frozen W1/W2 k1.finite-model/v1 require the finite proof artifact world domain to equal the claim world domain. B0 refuses to invent unobserved worlds merely to satisfy that proof-kind overconstraint. Multi-world local-witness binding remains a separate proof-kind gap.

world_commitment.preimage: ASCII RISU-K1-BINDING-B0-WORLD\x00 followed by B + netstring(exact world-input bytes)
world_commitment.authority: computed by the B0 binder; the target process cannot supply a world id

observation_contract.cut: After the target process exits or after the binder terminates it for timeout, the binder reads the complete sink file bytes exactly once.
observation_contract.stdout: non-authoritative diagnostic channel; never a consequence source
observation_contract.stderr: non-authoritative diagnostic channel; never a consequence source
observation_contract.exit_status: non-authoritative for regression grounding; an already-observed forbidden effect is not erased by nonzero exit
observation_contract.timeout: non-authoritative for an effect already durably present at the cut; timeout before any valid forbidden effect yields no authority
observation_contract.malformed_sink: UNKNOWN/NO_AUTHORITY; B0 does not cherry-pick valid-looking prefixes from an ambiguous sink

consequence_commitment.preimage: ASCII RISU-K1-BINDING-B0-CONSEQUENCE\x00 followed by K + netstring(kind) + S + netstring(subject) + V + netstring(value)
consequence_commitment.authority: computed by the B0 binder from strict sink parsing; the target process cannot supply a consequence id

implementation_commitment.meaning: B0 binds the observation to the exact executable bytes actually invoked, not merely to source text or a repository revision.

composition.finite_model_artifact: For a supported single-world run, B0 constructs a k1.finite-model/v1 artifact containing the set of valid consequences actually observed in that run. This artifact is not asserted to be an exhaustive model of all possible implementation behaviors.
composition.witness: If at least one observed consequence is outside ALLOW, B0 deterministically selects the lexicographically first forbidden (world, consequence) pair and constructs a normal W0 regression witness referencing the generated finite-model artifact.
composition.independent_consumers: The generated claim/artifact/witness must be accepted as REGRESSION by both frozen W1 and qualified W2. B0 invokes them as external CLIs and imports neither implementation.
composition.binding_result: Only the conjunction of direct implementation observation plus W1 acceptance plus W2 acceptance authorizes BOUND_REGRESSION.

producer_non_authority: The target cannot provide finite-model proof bytes.
The target cannot turn stdout/stderr text into semantic authority.
The target cannot obtain preservation authority from a clean or allowed observation.
success_rule: All precommitted vectors must meet their expected authority class.
The B0 binder must not import W1 or W2 and must invoke them only as external CLIs.
No pre-existing file in k1-w2-qualified may be modified, deleted, or renamed.
The target specimen source must be outside the binder and checker implementations.
The final hosted qualification must rebuild the target variants and W2, rerun all vectors, and verify exact pinned blobs.
A green B0 supports only observed-execution regression binding in the declared single-world finite-run scope.
explicit_non_claims: No preservation authority from black-box testing.
No proof that the executable is deterministic.
No proof that an observed finite model is exhaustive for the implementation.
No arbitrary-program sandbox or malicious-code containment claim.
